Bug_Title: FL: Do not use floating-point variables as loop counters (FL_FLOATS_AS_LOOP_COUNTERS)
Bug_Details: Using floating-point variables should not be used as loop counters, as they are not precise, which may result in incorrect loops. A loop counter is a variable that is changed with each iteration and controls when the loop should terminate. It is decreased or increased by a fixed amount each iteration. See rule NUM09-J.
Bug_Explanation: This code uses a floating-point variable 'i' as a loop counter, which is not precise and can lead to incorrect loop iterations. For example, when 'limit' is 1.0f, the loop will iterate 10 times instead of the expected 10 times because of floating-point precision issues.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by calling the showBug method with a limit of 1.0f. This causes the loop counter 'i' to increment by 0.1f in each iteration, resulting in 10 iterations instead of the expected 1 iteration due to floating-point precision issues.
